name: Tunis Carthage International Airport
before:
Tunisia's main airport and the capital's own, named after Carthage, which lies just to the east. It is the home base for Tunisair, Tunisair Express, Nouvelair and Tunisavia.

The site has been in aviation since 1920, when Tunisia's first seaplane base was built on the Lake of Tunis. A land airfield followed in 1938, carrying around 5,800 passengers a year on the Paris to Tunis run.

The Second World War made it important. The United States Twelfth Air Force used it as a headquarters and command base for the Italian campaign of 1943, and once the combat units moved on it became a major transshipment hub for cargo and personnel, a stop on the Cairo to Dakar route across North Africa.

The present airport was built from 1944 with French funding and became Tunisair's main hub in 1948, the airline flying DC-3s to Marseille, Rome, Algiers, Tripoli and down to Djerba and Sfax. Through the 1950s it was a regular stopover for Air France, TWA and others on long haul routes.

The Tunisian Civil Aviation and Airports Authority has its head office here.
after: Tunis-Carthage is Tunisia's main airport and the capital's own. It is the home base for Tunisair, and Tunisair Express and Nouvelair also fly from here.

claims.note: Main means busiest. OACA's 2024 figures, as Mosaique FM reported them on 5 January 2025, give Tunis-Carthage 7,249,701 of the 12.538 million passengers at all Tunisian airports, more than half; Djerba-Zarzis came next among OACA's airports with 2,203,957. TAV's two Tunisian airports, Monastir and Enfidha, handled 2,925,073 between them in 2024 and 3,198,931 in 2025 (TAV, 17 February 2026). The Wikipedia infobox has the same 7,249,701 for 2024. The name is written Tunis-Carthage by OACA's figures, Tunisair and Tunisair Express alike. No 2025 figure for Tunis-Carthage itself was found.
